title: Why do we procrastinate?
text: Procrastination is usually blamed {{1}} laziness, but psychologists disagree. Far {{2}} being idle, procrastinators are often perfectionists {{3}} fear that their work will not be good enough. Putting off a task gives short-term relief, {{4}} the guilt that follows makes the problem worse. Researchers recommend breaking large tasks {{5}} small, concrete steps, since vagueness fuels avoidance. {{6}} helps is setting a timer for just five minutes; starting is the hardest part, and momentum does the rest. It also helps to remove distractions {{7}} — leave the phone in another room. Most importantly, forgive yourself: studies show that students {{8}} forgave themselves for procrastinating procrastinated less afterwards.
